## The Connection

[[credential-scoping]] and [[runtime-paths]] are two expressions of the same architectural principle: **a single, centralized composition point at startup that determines what each component receives and cannot get elsewhere.**

In credential scoping, the Hub's secrets loader composes the Anthropic API key into the Ingest and Query agent child processes' environment at spawn time, never storing it in the Hub's own process. Each child process receives exactly what it needs, determined once, upstream.

In runtime paths, the Hub's startup path resolver composes every file-system location into a resolved path set at startup, and all downstream code consumes that preset configuration rather than discovering or recalculating paths on its own.

Both enforce **composition locality**: credentials and paths are not scattered across the codebase, and neither the Hub nor its child processes can later mutate or expand what they have access to beyond what was composed at startup. This prevents both accidental leakage (a compromised Hub cannot inspect the child process's environment) and architectural drift (no component can redefine its own resource scope).

## Why This Matters

The pattern guards against two failure modes:

1. **Scope creep**: without a single composition point, each component might discover or request additional resources at runtime, leading to inconsistent boundaries and harder-to-audit access.
2. **Implicit dependencies**: when resources are resolved locally (by reading environment or the ambient working directory), different parts of the system may end up with different values, and the actual configuration becomes invisible to auditing and testing.

By centralizing composition, Grimoire makes the resource boundary between parent and child, and between the system and each agent, an architectural invariant checked once at startup.

## Answer

Both [[credential-scoping]] and [[runtime-paths]] express the same core architectural principle: **a single, centralized composition point at startup that determines what each component receives and cannot get elsewhere.**

**Credential scoping** uses this for secrets: the Hub's secrets loader injects the Anthropic API key only into the child process environment at spawn time—never storing it in the Hub's own process. Each agent receives exactly what it needs, determined once upstream.

**Runtime paths** uses it for file locations: the Hub's startup path resolver composes every file-system location (wiki root, database, secrets file, agent directories) into a single resolved path set at startup, and all downstream code consumes that preset configuration rather than discovering paths dynamically.

The two decisions work together to enforce **scope as an architectural invariant**: resources are not scattered across the codebase, and neither the Hub nor its children can mutate or expand what they have access to beyond what was determined at startup. This guards against both accidental leakage (a compromised Hub cannot inspect what the child inherited) and scope creep (no component can redefine its own access by discovering additional resources at runtime).

I've saved this connection as a new page, [[concepts/single-composition-point]], since the relationship between these two decisions is genuinely new to the wiki and worth preserving as the architecture evolves.
